author: WP19
summary: Surveys CNA's oracles (real-XNA image corpus, tolerance policy, project goldens, point samples, the FNA value harness, independent oracles) and argues for choosing authority before tolerance. The XNA corpus itself was already covered in depth by the verification and xna-oracle pages; the golden harness semantics, tolerance distribution, point-sample counts, FNA comparator semantics, independent-oracle patterns and authority hierarchy are new on the oracles deep dive. Counts and renderer names were stale and corrected; the policy table belonged to a retired family.

Project-owned goldens answer a weaker question
Point samples and the skip boundary

concepts.text: A test does not yield a verdict until something defines the expected result; CNA uses captured real-XNA pixels, numeric values from a running FNA, renderer-to-renderer comparisons, independently recomputed mathematics and looser project-owned goldens, with deliberately different authority and tolerance.
tokens: Choose the authority before the tolerance

concepts.text: tools/xna-oracle holds 39 declarative scenes and 39 matching 256x256 reference PNGs captured once, by hand, from the real XNA 4.0 runtime under Wine (with DXVK); the C# runner source is committed but its executable, the XNA runtime and the private 32-bit prefix are not, and are needed only to regenerate references.
tokens: The images were captured once, by hand, and are committed

concepts.text: One renderer-agnostic C++ program implements the CNA side and is built into the DIRECTX9, EasyGL, FNA3D and Software trees.

The comparator uses absolute per-channel differences with a default tolerance of 0 and no PSNR, SSIM or perceptual metric; optional RGB and alpha tolerances, a raw-differing-pixel budget and an allowed rectangle make exceptions explicit instead of weakening the corpus globally.
concepts.note: xna-oracle takeover page also documents the flags ("--tolerance defaults to 0").

concepts.text: An increased tolerance needs a documented, scene-specific reason, because silent tolerance growth turns an authenticity project into a parity project.
tokens: exactly how an authenticity project quietly becomes a parity project

concepts.text: Gate strength by renderer: DIRECTX9's registered hard gate runs all 39 scenes at tolerance 0 and FNA3D's is a render-survival gate; the claim that EasyGL is only a manual measurement is corrected (EasyGL_XnaLineCoverage gates two line scenes exactly; Software_XnaLineCoverage renders the same two but fails only on a render failure), and the second GL runner the unit names belonged to a retired family.

concepts.section: A policy table is part of the oracle
concepts.text: The concrete per-scene tolerance policy table the unit describes served a renderer family that no longer exists; no runner at TARGET passes a policy file or any relaxation flag.
concepts.note: The policy TSV belonged to a retired renderer family (Bible ch70 policy-table section); it was deleted with that family. The generic rule is kept as the next concept.

concepts.section: A policy table is part of the oracle
concepts.text: Where a current renderer needs tolerance, the policy belongs beside the scenes with explicit RGB/alpha bounds, a maximum differing-pixel count and any permitted rectangle, and the runner should verify policy-to-scene set equality before comparing, keeping relaxation local, bounded and reviewable.
tokens: the policy's scene set equals the corpus's scene set

target.evidence: design rule; scripts/xna-diff.py offers the local flags, no runner uses them

concepts.section: Project-owned goldens answer a weaker question
concepts.text: PixelTestGame provides single-region expectations and full golden comparison for standalone renderer programs; both compare R, G and B and ignore alpha unless a test checks it explicitly, and an ExpectTrue precondition keeps a failed setup from being reported as a pixel result.
tokens: compares R, G and B only

concepts.section: Project-owned goldens answer a weaker question
concepts.text: Seventeen 8x8 golden PNGs live under examples/golden with EasyGL-derived names; the claim that another GL renderer reuses them is corrected: thirteen Vulkan registrations compile the EasyGL golden sources and compare against the same files.
concepts.note: The renderer the unit named is a retired identity; not written.

concepts.section: Project-owned goldens answer a weaker question
concepts.text: Golden tolerances range from 0 to 60 per channel (only the solid-blue canary is exact); at the high end the test catches gross shape or state regressions, and a self-captured golden is a regression oracle for CNA's chosen behaviour, not evidence of matching XNA.
tokens: not evidence that the behaviour matches XNA

concepts.section: Project-owned goldens answer a weaker question
concepts.text: Setting CNA_UPDATE_GOLDEN to any non-empty value rewrites the reference from the live render; updating is a review operation that should carry the diff, renderer, driver and reason, never a way to turn a failure green.
tokens: Updating is therefore a review operation

concepts.section: Point samples and the skip boundary
concepts.text: Single-pixel coverage is far broader than golden coverage; the unit's 340 calls in 70 files and 169 including sources are stale: TARGET has 225 ExpectPixel call sites in 49 C++ files and 119 sources that include the harness.
tokens: 225 ExpectPixel( call sites in 49 C++ files

concepts.section: Point samples and the skip boundary
concepts.text: The harness probes SDL video before running and returns 77, which CTest reports as skipped; a green headless run can mean none of the comparisons executed, so pixel reports must state display and skip evidence.

A separate chain runs C# against a live FNA.dll and compares its JSON with CNA's reference dump over enums, state presets, packed vectors and viewport cases; numbers compare at absolute 1e-4, everything else exactly, and the walk is one-directional (every FNA key must exist on the CNA side, CNA-only keys are ignored). It is manual, not a CTest.

Worked historical case: the manual comparison found IndexElementSize using semantic values 16/32 where FNA uses 0/1, after first exposing three defects in the harness itself; the divergence was fixed on 2026-07-09 and CNA now declares SixteenBits = 0 and ThirtyTwoBits = 1, showing a second implementation challenging the public value surface without any pixels.
concepts.note: Published only as a clearly historical worked case with the current enum values.

concepts.text: Golden tables: packed-vector expected values are derived separately (in Python from FNA's bit-packing formulas) and checked with narrow tolerances; the genuine-framework packing oracle outranks them where they differ.

Recomputation ladders: the glTF oracle helpers rebuild accessor (L2), vertex-stream (L3) and world-position (L4) results independently of the production routine against manifest values, and their own acceptance tests prove the oracle does not change production output.

Shared oracle headers: one analytically derived reference is included by several renderers' tests so copies cannot drift, e.g. the transformed-camera fog scenes shared by EasyGL, SDL_GPU, Vulkan and a neutral contract test.
LZX decompression has a byte-exact differential against output produced by FNA's unmodified decoder under Mono, with checked-in reference bytes.
concepts.note: The unit adds that this differential once exposed a heap-buffer overflow; no TARGET source or test records that history, so it is not published (unverifiable).

concepts.text: Cross-renderer controls: a small 64x64 diagnostic corpus with a bounded renderer-to-renderer tolerance and an explicit whitelist of excluded, legitimately divergent constructs; excluding unstable cases beats widening the tolerance. At TARGET the 2D corpus is built for Direct2D, EasyGL and Vulkan and the 3D scene for EasyGL, Vulkan, Software and WebGPU, compared by cna_diag_compare at a default tolerance of 40.
tokens: Excluding unstable constructs is preferable to widening the tolerance
concepts.note: The unit names only Direct2D and EasyGL.

concepts.text: Authority hierarchy: real XNA defines authenticity, a live FNA is an independent compatibility reference, independent mathematics checks algorithms, cross-renderer controls localise implementation defects and CNA-owned goldens prevent unintended change; tolerance follows the authority and phenomenon, and "passed the oracle" is incomplete without which oracle, which policy and whether it ran.
tokens: is incomplete until the reader knows which oracle

concepts.text: Claim that CNA does not reference the sibling decompiled-XNA or converted-specification repositories: seventeen test files cite decompiled XNA sources in comments as the basis of expected values, though no script or gate reads either repository.

target.evidence: rg -l "xna4-decomp|xna4-spec" modules (17 test files, comments only)

issues.text: Software_XnaLineCoverage exits non-zero only on a render failure or missing reference; pixel differences print DIFF and still pass.
